answer: Agents can limit rewards to participants that post a refundable stake and pass a randomly assigned, delayed task whose result is checked against independent agents’ work. A new identity must lock real value before it can earn, while splitting one agent into many does not improve the chance of passing the task; coordinated answers also risk conflicting with the independent signal. The rule works like a reef around an ivory tower: not proof of a person, but a costly barrier. An attacker pays capital costs, waits, and risks forfeiting stakes for failed identities.
